thread.title: What to Watch: Pound surges, Bank of England in focus, Shell stock slips

author: Alanna Petroff
title: What to Watch: Pound surges, Bank of England in focus, Shell stock slips
text:
The UK pound was rising on Thursday morning against the euro and US dollar. Photo: Omar Marques/Getty Images More Here’s a daily overview of the top business, market and economic developments to watch in the UK, Europe and abroad:
Pound rebound Sterling extended its gains on Thursday morning after the Times newspaper reported that British Prime Minister Theresa May had sealed a tentative deal with Brussels on financial services.
The pound jumped to trade just over $1.29 against the US dollar, up about two cents since early Wednesday. It also surged against the euro to trade around €1.14.
On Wednesday, Brexit minister Dominic Raab said he expected a Brexit deal with Brussels to be concluded by November 21. The British government later said there was no set date for Brexit talks to finish.
Expectations for the Bank of England The pound could post further swings on Thursday afternoon in reaction to moves by Britain’s central bank. The Bank of England (BoE) is expected to keep interest rates steady on Thursday at noon local time and then host a press conference headed by governor Mark Carney. It’s also releasing its latest inflation report and forecasts.
A year ago the BoE raised interest rates for the first time since the global financial crisis and followed this with a further rise in borrowing costs to 0.75% in August.
Economists polled by Reuters expect the nine members of the BoE’s Monetary Policy Committee to have voted unanimously to keep rates on hold this month, and on average do not see a further rate rise until May.
Deutsche Bank economists “expect governor Carney to talk up market pricing of a rate hike next year on the back of stronger wage and output growth” in the third quarter, the German bank said in a research report.
Stocks post tentative gains European stock markets were posting tentative gains on Thursday. The DAX ( ^GDAXI ) in Germany and the CAC40 ( ^FCHI ) in France were rising a tad. The UK’s FTSE 100 ( ^FTSE ) was essentially flat, held back by a drop in the shares of oil giants Royal Dutch Shell ( RDSB.L ) and BP ( BP.L ).
Royal Dutch Shell reported on Thursday an almost 40% rise in third-quarter profit to $5.6bn as it benefited from rising crude prices. But the results still fell short of forecasts and the shares were down by about 2.5% in early trading in London.
Asian markets were mostly positive on Thursday, though the Nikkei 225 ( ^N225 ) dropped by 1.1%.
What to expect in the US US stock futures were edging higher on Thursday as investors await earnings from a range of companies, including Sotheby’s ( BID ) and Spotify ( SPOT ) before the opening bell. Apple ( AAPL ) and Starbucks ( SBUX ) are among the the main companies reporting results after the close.
With files from Reuters
